questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Feeling of being in a place before having already experienced the present situation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Deja-vu"** refers to the feeling that one has lived through the present situation before. (पहले भी देखा हुआ)

 
 
• **Example:** As she walked into the old house, she experienced a strong sense of **deja-vu.**
 
 
 
• **"Deja-vu"** is a **French term** that literally means **"already seen"**. It is commonly used to describe a situation where a person feels that they have already experienced the present moment. (पहले से देखा हुआ)
 
 
• **Example:** He felt a strange sense of **deja-vu** when he met her for the first time.
 
 

Therefore, the correct one word substitution for the given phrase is **'Deja-vu.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Illusion** (भ्रम): A false idea or belief, or something that appears to be something that it is not.

 
 
• **Example:** The magician created the** illusion** of a disappearing rabbit.
 
 
 
• **Spirituality** (आध्यात्मिकता): The quality of being concerned with the human spirit or soul as opposed to material or physical things.
 
 
• **Example:** She found comfort in her **spirituality **during difficult times.
 
 
 
• **Delusion** (मोह): A belief or impression that is firmly maintained despite being contradicted by what is generally accepted as reality or rational argument.
 
 
• **Example:** His belief that he could fly was a dangerous **delusion.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

My grandmother helps us in all the problems. She has __a remedy for all the diseases.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'panacea' **means a solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases.
 
• It is the most appropriate option to replace the underlined words **'has a remedy for all the diseases.'**
 
• Option 1** 'Service'** means assistance or help, but it does not convey the meaning of a remedy for diseases.
 
• Option 3** 'Fanatic'** means a person filled with excessive enthusiasm, which is not relevant here.
 
• Option 4** 'Heretic' **refers to someone who goes against established beliefs, also irrelevant to the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence: *"My grandmother helps us in all the problems. She is a panacea for all the diseases."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A:** Panacea is often used metaphorically to suggest someone or something can solve all problems or difficulties.
 
• **B:** Its usage here is to emphasize the grandmother's ability to provide solutions in all situations.
 
• **C:** The term 'panacea' originates from Greek mythology, where Panacea was the goddess of universal remedy.
